Visual development studies

Three independent concepts

Three independent, fictional treatment concepts made with AI-generated imagery. The people and locations pictured are illustrative; the contributors and access described in the pages are proposed. Commissioned client work remains private while display permission is checked.

“produces beautifully original and glossy pitch decks”Owen Phillips, Executive Producer · on commissioned work
01 / Independent concept

What Remains

An industrial town cover opens into a proposed film about work, family and who shapes a place’s future.

Read proposed page text

When the shift ends

We will follow three generations of a steel town through the decisions that will shape its next chapter: a worker approaching the end of his working life, a young person deciding whether to leave, and a family trying to keep a business open.

The film moves between kitchens, union meetings and the routines of the high street. Personal photographs and local archive will bring the town's industrial past into the present. As competing promises emerge, we will ask who has a voice in the future and who is expected to live with the consequences.

02 / Independent concept

The Paper Trail

A bound case file opens into a proposed investigation of a public decision and the records behind it.

Explore the interactive treatment↗
Read proposed page text

Who signed it off?

The investigation begins with a public decision and the people living with its consequences. We will reconstruct how it was reached, following meeting minutes, correspondence and the accounts of those who were in the room.

Each chapter tests a different part of the official explanation. Interviews will be set against the contemporaneous record; unanswered questions will guide further reporting. Those whose decisions come under scrutiny will be invited to respond. The tension comes from watching an apparently settled story become less certain, one document at a time.

03 / Independent concept

The Last Trace

An ordinary crossing opens into a proposed story assembled from remembered moments and tested records.

Read proposed page text

The last known journey

We begin with a journey that can only be reconstructed in fragments. A remembered conversation. An image caught on camera. A time that does not quite fit. The film will follow the reporting as those fragments are assembled and tested.

People closest to the missing person will lead the story. We will revisit key locations with contributors, distinguish contemporary records from later recollections, and keep uncertainty visible. Patient observational filming will sit alongside carefully contextualised archive. Our aim is to understand a life and the questions left behind, without turning speculation into fact.
